title: RRB Station Master CBT · Foundation model 1
note: 100-question model with foundational Maths and Science, applied data analysis and multi-step reasoning. Uses the indicative 30/30/20/20 distribution.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: What is the HCF of 84 and 126?
questions.explanation: 84 = 2 × 42 and 126 = 3 × 42; 2 and 3 are coprime.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: What is the LCM of 18 and 24?
questions.explanation: Use the highest prime powers: 2³ × 3² = 72.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A quantity increases from 240 to 300. What is the percentage increase?
questions.explanation: Increase 60 divided by original 240 gives 25%.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A sum is divided in the ratio 3:5. If the larger share is ₹250, what is the total?
questions.explanation: One part is 50; eight parts total 400.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The average of five numbers is 18. Removing 10 leaves what average?
questions.explanation: Total 90 minus 10 is 80; divide by four.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An item costing ₹800 is sold for ₹920. Find profit percent.
questions.explanation: Profit 120 divided by cost 800 gives 15%.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A ₹1,500 marked price receives a 20% discount. What is paid?

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Find simple interest on ₹2,000 at 6% annually for three years.
questions.explanation: Interest = principal × rate × years / 100.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: At 10% compounded annually, ₹1,000 becomes what after two years?

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A train covers 180 km in 2.5 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = distance / time = 180 / 2.5.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Convert 54 km/h to metres per second.
questions.explanation: Multiply by 5/18.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A can finish work in 12 days and B in 6 days. Together they need how long?
questions.explanation: Their combined daily rate is 1/12 + 1/6 = 1/4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Solve 3x + 7 = 28.
questions.explanation: Subtract 7 and divide by 3.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: If x + y = 12 and x − y = 4, find x.
questions.explanation: Adding the equations gives 2x = 16.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Find the tenth term of 5, 8, 11, ...

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Find the sum of the first ten positive integers.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A rectangle is 12 m long and 7 m wide. Find its area.
questions.explanation: Area = length × width.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Find a circle's circumference for radius 7 cm, using π = 22/7.
questions.explanation: Circumference = 2πr.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A cube has side 4 cm. Find its volume.
questions.explanation: Volume = side cubed.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: In a right triangle, sides opposite and adjacent to angle θ are 3 and 4. Find tan θ.
questions.explanation: Tangent is opposite divided by adjacent.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A fair die is rolled once. What is the probability of an even number?
questions.explanation: Three of six outcomes are even.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Find the median of 3, 5, 8, 10, 14.
questions.explanation: The middle of five ordered observations is the third value.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: One newton accelerates one kilogram by one metre per second squared.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A body has mass 5 kg. With g = 10 m/s², its weight is what?
questions.explanation: Weight = mass × gravitational acceleration.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 200 g object occupies 50 cm³. Find density.
questions.explanation: Density = mass / volume.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A force of 10 N moves an object 5 m in the force direction. Find work.
questions.explanation: Work = force × distance along force.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A machine does 600 J of work in 3 seconds. Find power.
questions.explanation: Power = work / time.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Find kinetic energy of a 2 kg body travelling at 3 m/s.
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy = one half × mass × speed squared.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 12 V source is connected across a 6 Ω resistor. Find current.
questions.explanation: Ohm's law: I = V/R.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An ideal lever has effort arm 60 cm and load arm 20 cm. Find mechanical advantage.
questions.explanation: For an ideal lever, mechanical advantage is effort arm / load arm.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: At which load is the observation furthest above the fitted reference line?
questions.explanation: The line rises two minutes per ten crates. All plotted observations lie on it except the 30-crate observation, which is higher.
questions.passage: For this trial, a fitted comparison line through the observations at 10 and 60 crates is used as a reference. Deviation means observed minus fitted time. The sample contains one observation per load.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: By how many minutes does the observed time at 30 crates exceed the fitted value?
questions.explanation: Interpolate between the endpoints: at 30 crates the fit predicts 41. The point is at 48, a positive difference of 7.
questions.passage: For this trial, a fitted comparison line through the observations at 10 and 60 crates is used as a reference. Deviation means observed minus fitted time. The sample contains one observation per load.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: The pattern is used to estimate the effect of moving from 60 to 70 crates. What is the important qualification?
options: Using a fitted line proves the time will follow it exactly.
An unusual point below 60 rules out every estimate at 70.
The estimated trend is being extended beyond the observed load range.
The mean observed dispatch time is automatically the estimate at 70.
questions.explanation: The plot ends at 60 crates. The fit can be extended, but it has not been verified at higher loads.
questions.passage: For this trial, a fitted comparison line through the observations at 10 and 60 crates is used as a reference. Deviation means observed minus fitted time. The sample contains one observation per load.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Which summary is unaffected if the 30-crate recorded time is corrected upward by a further five minutes?
options: The fitted line based on the two specified endpoints.
questions.explanation: The reference line uses only the 10- and 60-crate observations. The 30-crate correction changes its residual, the overall mean and the maximum.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: If clue 1 is dropped and all other clues still apply, how many orders are possible?
questions.explanation: Retain all clues except 1. The remaining constraints admit 20 distinct permutations, including the original order. Count arrangements with position 1 fixed before moving to the next permitted first item.
questions.passage:
Five activities occupy successive slots, one per slot, with no breaks between slots.
1. Mapping immediately follows Packing, and Weighing immediately follows Dispatch.
2. Labelling is earlier than Dispatch but later than Mapping.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Between 3:00 and the first overlap after it, when is the smaller angle between the clock hands 18.5°?
questions.explanation: On this side of the overlap the separation is 30 × 3 − 5.5m. Set that equal to 18.5 and solve for m = 13.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A register is inspected on a Tuesday. Its next inspection is due 31 days later, but it is carried out two days after the due date. On which weekday is the inspection carried out?
questions.explanation: The actual interval is 33 days. Its remainder on division by seven is 5. Advance that many weekdays from Tuesday.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Farah and Gita are sisters. The second sister’s husband has a son from an earlier marriage and a daughter with her. What is the first sister’s relationship to that daughter?
questions.explanation: The girl’s mother is the second sister. The mother’s sister is the maternal aunt. The earlier child is unrelated to that identification.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Five containers weigh 5, 7, 10, 14, 20 kg. A loading bay accepts exactly two whose combined weight is exactly 25 kg. The heavier selected container is loaded first. Which weight is loaded second?
questions.explanation: Testing pairs against the capacity leaves 20 + 5 = 25. In descending weight order the second is 5 kg.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A lamp is already on. Each pulse reverses its state. It receives 4 pulses before a pause, then 6 more pulses. During maintenance the technician manually toggles it once and disconnects it before any further pulse. What was its state immediately before the manual toggle and immediately afterwards?
questions.explanation: The total number of automatic toggles is 10. Each pair cancels. The manual toggle then reverses the state once more.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question:
Exactly one of Farah, Gita, Hema is assigned a report, and exactly 2 of the following claims are true.
1. Farah is assigned the report.
2. Gita is assigned the report.
3. Gita is not assigned the report.
Who receives the report?
questions.explanation: Test the three possible recipients. Assigning the report to Farah makes 2 claims true; assigning it to Gita makes 1 claims true; assigning it to Hema makes 1 claims true. Only Farah yields the required count.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An audit reviews 20 requests. A request can pass only if both its date and fare are verified. All requests with verified fares have reference codes. Exactly 5 requests lack a code and 7 requests lack date verification. The two groups overlap in two cases. What is the largest possible number of passes?
questions.explanation: Any request without a code lacks fare verification and therefore fails. The union of the two groups is 5 + 7 − 2 = 10 requests. At most 20 − 10 can pass, and that is possible if all other requests meet both requirements.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Five applicants Omar, Rahul, Sahil, Tara and Uma are each on at least one of two lists. List X has three names and List Y has three names. X includes Omar and Rahul; Y includes Sahil and Tara. Both lists exclude the two names already given for the other list. Who must appear on both?
questions.explanation: The given members are exclusive. The only remaining applicant, Uma, must fill the third place on both lists.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A surveyor starts facing north, goes 12 m forward, turns left and goes 5 m, then turns left again and goes 9 m. Ignoring obstacles, which displacement from the start is correct?
questions.explanation: The first and third walks are opposite, leaving 12 − 9 = 3 m along the original heading. The middle walk is to the left of the starting direction.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Exactly two of Omar, Rahul, Sahil and Tara are on leave. Omar is on leave if and only if Sahil is on leave. Tara is working. The two people at work must cover reception and records, one duty each. Tara covers records. Who covers reception?
questions.explanation: Because Tara is working and exactly two people are on leave, the paired leave status must put Omar and Sahil on leave. The working pair is Rahul and Tara.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Team P inspected 10 boxes and team Q inspected 5 boxes. Exactly 7 of all inspected boxes were rejected. Each team inspected a disjoint set. What is the minimum possible number of rejections from P?
questions.explanation: At most 5 rejections can come from Q because Q inspected only 5. That leaves at least 2 among P. The minimum is attainable if every Q box was rejected.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A committee selects exactly two of reports Omar, Rahul, Sahil and Tara. Selecting Omar forces Sahil. Selecting Tara rules out Sahil. New rules also forbid choosing Rahul together with Sahil, and forbid choosing Rahul together with Tara. Which pair can be selected?
questions.explanation: Any pair containing Omar must also contain Sahil. Without Omar, all three possible pairs among Rahul, Sahil and Tara breach a prohibition. The single valid pair is Omar–Sahil.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Two workshops report fewer errors after a common training session. Only one workshop replaced unreliable equipment at the same time. Which comparison best isolates the equipment change?
options: Compare both workshops’ new error totals without adjusting for work volumes.
Compare workers who volunteered for the training with those who attended once.
Compare changes in error rates for equivalent work across both workshops over the same dates.
Use only the workshop receiving new equipment and count the number of repairs.
questions.explanation: The shared training can affect both. Comparing changes for equivalent work highlights a difference specific to the equipment workshop, subject to comparable conditions.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A quality screen catches almost all faulty items but also flags many sound ones. A clerk asserts that almost every flagged item is faulty. Which fact is most relevant to testing that assertion?
options: The number of separate inspectors who operate the screen.
The proportion of all inspected items that were faulty before screening.
The order in which faulty items entered the inspection room.
Whether the screen flags multiple defects on one item under the same code.
questions.explanation: The mix of faulty and sound items determines the numbers of true and false flags. A low underlying fault rate can produce many false flags despite high sensitivity.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which order satisfies every clue, from position 1 to position 5?
questions.explanation: Checking the stated restrictions leaves only Bronze → Dusk → Amber → Copper → Ember. Bronze → Dusk → Amber → Ember → Copper violates clue 3. Copper → Bronze → Dusk → Amber → Ember violates clue 3. Copper → Ember → Bronze → Dusk → Amber violates clue 3.
questions.passage:
Five sealed art crates are displayed in positions one to five, counted from the entrance.
1. Amber is exactly two positions after Bronze.
2. Dusk is immediately before Amber.
3. Copper is before Ember but after Amber.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which claim best captures the engineer’s argument?
options: The repaired well gives a reliable estimate of the effect of terracing alone.
Use a comparison well before attributing the full increase to the repair.
A similar increase in both wells would establish that the repairs had no effect.
The repair and terracing effects can be distinguished by measuring the repaired well more often.
questions.explanation: Both changes could improve retention. A comparable unrepaired well provides evidence about the influence they share.
questions.passage: A village repaired an old stepwell after a series of dry summers. During the first monsoon, water remained in the well longer than villagers remembered. An engineer noticed that the repair had closed several cracks, but she also found that the fields uphill had recently been terraced. The terraces slowed runoff and could have allowed more water to reach the underground reservoir. She recommended measuring water levels in a nearby unrepaired well served by the same slope. If both wells gained similarly, the terraces deserved more credit than a visitor looking only at the repaired well might award them.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which result would most strengthen the case that sealing the cracks made a separate contribution?
options: Both wells gain equally after the terraces are built.
The repaired well already held more water than the comparison well before either change.
The repaired well gains substantially more than the comparison well after similar rainfall.
Rain is heavier near the repaired well than near the comparison well.
questions.explanation: The gain rather than the level matters. A larger gain at the repaired site under similar rainfall supports a separate repair effect.
questions.passage: A village repaired an old stepwell after a series of dry summers. During the first monsoon, water remained in the well longer than villagers remembered. An engineer noticed that the repair had closed several cracks, but she also found that the fields uphill had recently been terraced. The terraces slowed runoff and could have allowed more water to reach the underground reservoir. She recommended measuring water levels in a nearby unrepaired well served by the same slope. If both wells gained similarly, the terraces deserved more credit than a visitor looking only at the repaired well might award them.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: How does the final sentence advance the passage?
options: It explains how one possible measurement would affect the attribution.
It supplies the measurement that confirms the engineer’s prediction.
It replaces the proposed comparison with a different research method.
It identifies the physical route by which water enters the reservoir.
questions.explanation: The final sentence interprets a hypothetical outcome. The proposed comparison has yet to be carried out.
questions.passage: A village repaired an old stepwell after a series of dry summers. During the first monsoon, water remained in the well longer than villagers remembered. An engineer noticed that the repair had closed several cracks, but she also found that the fields uphill had recently been terraced. The terraces slowed runoff and could have allowed more water to reach the underground reservoir. She recommended measuring water levels in a nearby unrepaired well served by the same slope. If both wells gained similarly, the terraces deserved more credit than a visitor looking only at the repaired well might award them.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What assumption matters most in selecting the comparison well?
options: Both wells held exactly the same volume in each summer before repair.
A terrace assessment is more reliable in a village with several repaired wells.
Each well is used by the same number of households during the dry season.
Terracing can affect recharge to both wells through a comparable drainage area.
questions.explanation: The proposed comparison works only if the unrepaired well is exposed to the suspected common cause.
questions.passage: A village repaired an old stepwell after a series of dry summers. During the first monsoon, water remained in the well longer than villagers remembered. An engineer noticed that the repair had closed several cracks, but she also found that the fields uphill had recently been terraced. The terraces slowed runoff and could have allowed more water to reach the underground reservoir. She recommended measuring water levels in a nearby unrepaired well served by the same slope. If both wells gained similarly, the terraces deserved more credit than a visitor looking only at the repaired well might award them.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete both blanks in this sequence: 5, 25, 7, 24, 11, 21, __, __.
questions.explanation: Odd positions increase by consecutive even numbers (+2, +4, +6). Even positions decrease by consecutive odd numbers (−1, −3, −5).

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the missing interior term in 5, 7, ?, 19, 35, 67, 131.
questions.explanation: The gaps double: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64. Add 4 to the second term to get 11.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The six readings are 5, 9, 25, 29, 61, 65. The gaps alternate an unchanged increment with an increasing increment forming an arithmetic progression. What is the sum of the seventh and eighth readings?
questions.explanation: The changing gaps go 16, 32, 48, interleaved with +4. The seventh reading is 113. Add it to the eighth, which is 4 higher.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: On odd positions a code advances the letter by 2. On even positions it uses A↔Z, B↔Y, and so on. Which plain word produces VFNRR?
questions.explanation: Move odd-position letters backward by the stated shift. Mirroring is its own inverse at even positions.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A code transforms PLUME into GKSJR. First it shifts the two end letters forward by 2 and the three inside letters back by 2. What does the same code produce for TULIP, if it then reverses the shifted letters?
questions.explanation: The shifted intermediate word is VSJGR. Its reversal is RGJSV.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a cipher PLUME becomes RNTOD and GUIDE becomes ITHFD. The rule depends on whether the original letter is a vowel. How is TULIP encoded?
questions.explanation: From the examples, a vowel goes back one letter, and a consonant goes forward two letters. Classify each original letter separately.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: To encode a word, write its last, first and middle letters in that order as alphabet positions (A = 1). Replace each successive number after the first with its sum with the preceding original number. If the result is 16 / 36 / 32, what are the original first, middle and last letters in that order?
questions.explanation: The first displayed number gives the last letter. Subtract it from the second number to recover the first letter. Subtract the recovered first-letter value from the third to recover the middle letter.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A five-letter code sends PLUME to QNXQJ and PLANT to QNDRY. What code does it give TULIP?
questions.explanation: Reading two examples reveals successive shifts +1, +2, +3, +4 and +5. Apply those position shifts to TULIP and wrap after Z.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: For a two-digit number with unequal digits, 27 corresponds to 45 and 41 corresponds to 27. The output is the positive difference between the number and its reversal. Which input has the same output as 36?
questions.explanation: The difference is nine times the absolute digit gap. 3 and 6 differ by 3; both digits can increase by one without changing that gap.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In each pair (p,q) value one place apart gives (4,5) → 9 and (7,8) → 15. Check also (5,8) → 39. Under the same relation, what is (8,11)?
questions.explanation: The relation is q² − p² = (q − p)(q + p). The three-unit gap multiplies the sum of the two entries.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The rule sends 4 to 17, 7 to 47, and 9 to 77. It multiplies each input by one less than itself and adds a fixed constant. Which input gives 17?
questions.explanation: The examples establish the constant as 5. Subtract it from the target, then identify the adjacent factors. The larger factor is the input.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A machine transforms 18 to 6 and 50 to 10 by replacing an integer with the product of its distinct prime factors. If 96 is passed through the machine, and its output is passed through again, what is the final result?
questions.explanation: The first pass multiplies one copy of each distinct prime to give 6. The second pass sees exactly those same primes, each already present once.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Pairs 4 → 10 and 5 → 16 use the same rule. The rule uses the sum of the first n positive numbers, adjusted only when n is odd. Which output is paired with 12?
questions.explanation: An even input gives n(n+1)/2. The odd example is one larger than its triangular number, so add one only when the new input is odd.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a row of 41, H is 10th from the left and J is 14th from the right, with J right of H. Three people between them leave. Two new people join left of H. How many now stand between H and J?
questions.explanation: J began at position 28 from the left, so the gap contained 17 people. Only the three removals affect that gap.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: H ranks 17th in a preliminary list. The final list removes two people originally above H and adds 5 new entries. The number of new entries above H is half the new entries, rounded down. What is H’s final rank?
questions.explanation: Remove two higher ranks and add the stated number of newly higher ranks. Removed or added entries below H do not change H’s position.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Six runners have distinct times. S is faster than W but slower than T and P. U is faster than T and P is slower than T. W is faster than V. If the times of T and W are swapped, who is at rank 2, where rank 1 is fastest?
questions.explanation: The original order is U, T, P, S, W, V. The swap gives U, W, P, S, T, V. Read rank 2 from the new order.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a list of 41, K ranks 10th from the front and L ranks 14th from the rear. M ranks midway between them, counting positions. If their two positions have different parity, use the central position closer to K. What is M’s rank from the rear?
questions.explanation: L is at position 28 from the front. The lower of the central positions is 19. Convert it to the reverse rank by subtracting from 41 and adding 1.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A list ranks higher score first. For tied scores, earlier submission wins. K scores 17 at 09:21, L scores 28 at 09:24, M scores 28 at 09:18, and N scores 17 at 09:14. Two entries from each score band are initially listed. If M’s time is corrected to 09:29, which consecutive pair occupies places 2 and 3, in order?
questions.explanation: L now leads M in the higher-score band. N leads K in the lower-score band. The order is L, M, N, K.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a queue of 41, H is 10th from the front and J is 14th from the back. They swap places and everyone faces the other way, reversing which end is the front. How many people are ahead of J in the new direction?
questions.explanation: J moves to H’s old position. Under reversal the 31 people formerly behind that slot are now ahead.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: One term in 10, 14, 30, 36, 54, 66 was copied incorrectly. For the original sequence, at position n start with n² + 5n, then add 4 on odd positions. Which value needs replacing?
questions.explanation: Calculate the expected values at positions 1 through 6. The value at position 3 should be 28, two less than the listed value.

title: RRB Station Master CBT · Practice model 2
note: Full-length CBT practice with multi-step maths and science, shared data sets, English comprehension and reasoning. Uses the indicative 30/30/20/20 breakdown of CEN 08/2026.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An 18 L mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 3:2. How much water should be added to make the two quantities equal?
questions.explanation: Each of the five parts is 3.6 L. Milk exceeds water by one part, so add 3.6 L of water.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two positive integers have HCF 12 and LCM 1,260. One integer is 84. What is the other?
questions.explanation: The product of the two integers is 12 × 1,260. Dividing by 84 gives 180.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A trader bought an item for ₹640 and sold it for ₹720 after successive discounts of 10% and 20% off its marked price. What was the marked price?
questions.explanation: The sale price is 0.9 × 0.8 = 0.72 of the marked price. Thus the price before the discounts was 720/0.72.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The mean mass of 24 parcels is 50 kg. Four parcels with a mean mass of 65 kg are removed. What is the mean mass of the remaining parcels?
questions.explanation: The remaining mass is 24×50−4×65 = 940 kg for 20 parcels.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A needs 15 days to complete a job and B needs 20 days. They work together for 6 days. A then leaves. How many more days does B need?
questions.explanation: They complete 6(1/15+1/20) = 7/10 of the work. B completes the remaining 3/10 in 6 days.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A vehicle travels from P to Q at 48 km/h and returns by the same route at 72 km/h. Find its average speed for the complete trip.
questions.explanation: For equal distances the average is 2/(1/48+1/72) = 57.6 km/h.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 150 m train clears a 350 m bridge in 20 s. It then overtakes a cyclist moving at 5 m/s in the same direction. How many seconds does the train take to pass the cyclist?
questions.explanation: The train speed is (150+350)/20 = 25 m/s. Relative to the cyclist it gains 20 m/s, so passing takes 150/20 = 7.5 s.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A counter sells 70 tickets. Adult tickets cost ₹50 and child tickets cost ₹30. The total is ₹2,980. How many adult tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: If all tickets were child tickets, the total would be ₹2,100. Each adult ticket adds ₹20. The ₹880 difference represents 44 adult tickets.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The fourth and tenth terms of an arithmetic progression are 23 and 53. What is the sum of the first 15 terms?
questions.explanation: The common difference is (53−23)/6 = 5. The first and fifteenth terms are 8 and 78, so their sum over 15 terms is 15(8+78)/2.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: What is the remainder when 7 to the power 103 is divided by 5?
questions.explanation: Seven is congruent to 2 modulo 5. The remainders of powers of 2 cycle through 2, 4, 3, 1. Exponent 103 is 3 modulo 4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A box has 5 red, 4 blue and 3 green tokens. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that exactly one is red?
questions.explanation: Select one red and one of the seven nonred tokens in 35 ways. All unordered pairs number 12×11/2 = 66.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 32 m by 24 m rectangular courtyard is surrounded by a 2 m wide path outside its boundary. The outer boundary is rectangular. What is the area of the path?
questions.explanation: The outer dimensions are 36 m by 28 m. Subtract the courtyard area from 1,008 m² to get 240 m².

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 12 m vertical pole casts a 16 m shadow on level ground. What is the sine of the angle of elevation from the shadow tip to the pole top?
questions.explanation: The right triangle has sides 12, 16 and 20. The sine is opposite over hypotenuse, or 12/20.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A solid cylinder of radius 6 cm and height 20 cm is melted into identical spheres of radius 3 cm without loss. How many spheres can be made?
questions.explanation: The cylinder volume is 720π cm³. Each sphere has volume 36π cm³, so the count is 20.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: The five observations 6, 8, 10, 12 and 14 have their smallest value replaced by 20. What are the new mean and median respectively?
questions.explanation: The new sum is 50−6+20 = 64. The sorted values are 8, 10, 12, 14 and 20, so the middle value is 12.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two pieces of different materials each have mass 300 g. Their densities are 2 and 5 g/cm³. If combined without voids or volume change, what is their overall density?
questions.explanation: Volume is 300/2 + 300/5 = 210 cm³ and mass is 600 g. Their ratio is 20/7 g/cm³.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An object weighs 147 N where gravitational acceleration is 9.8 m/s². What are its mass and weight at a site where the acceleration is 1.6 m/s²?
questions.explanation: The mass is 147/9.8 = 15 kg everywhere. At the second site it weighs 15×1.6 = 24 N.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 10 kg box rests on a level floor. Its coefficient of static friction is 0.30 and g = 10 m/s². A horizontal pull of 26 N is applied. What friction force acts on it?
questions.explanation: Static friction adjusts to balance the 26 N pull because the required force is below the 30 N limit.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 4 kg object speeds up from 3 m/s to 7 m/s. What is the net work done on it?
questions.explanation: The work–energy theorem gives ΔK = ½ × 4 × (49−9) = 80 J.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A motor raises a 50 kg load through 6 m in 20 s at steady speed. With g = 10 m/s² and efficiency of 75%, what is the input power?
questions.explanation: Useful power is 50×10×6/20 = 150 W. Since that is 75% of input, the motor takes 200 W.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An ideal lever raises a 240 N load vertically by 5 cm. The effort point moves 20 cm in the direction of the applied force. What effort force is required?
questions.explanation: Equal input and output work gives effort × 20 = 240 × 5 in N·cm.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 600 W heater operates for 2 minutes. Seventy percent of its energy heats 0.4 kg of water of specific heat capacity 4,200 J/(kg·°C). What is the temperature rise?
questions.explanation: The water receives 0.7×600×120 = 50,400 J. Dividing by 0.4×4,200 gives a rise of 30°C.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 12 Ω resistor and an 8 Ω resistor are connected in parallel across 24 V. When the 12 Ω branch is disconnected, by what percentage does the supply current decrease?
questions.explanation: The two initial currents are 2 A and 3 A. The supply current drops from 5 A to 3 A, a 40% decrease.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 900 W heater runs 40 minutes daily for 14 days. How much electrical energy does it use?
questions.explanation: Convert to 0.9 kW and 2/3 hour daily. The product 0.9×2/3×14 is 8.4 kWh.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 10 kg trolley starts from rest. Forces of 28 N east and 8 N west act on it for 4 s. What speed does it reach?
questions.explanation: The net force is 20 N east, so the acceleration is 2 m/s². In 4 s it gains 8 m/s of speed.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A sheet measures 18 cm by 25 cm with a thickness of 3.6 mm. What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Convert 3.6 mm to 0.36 cm before multiplying 18×25×0.36.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A liquid has density 1.2 g/cm³. What is the mass of 1.5 L of the liquid?
questions.explanation: The volume is 1,500 cm³, giving mass of 1,800 g or 1.8 kg.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A linear thermometer shows 5 units in melting ice and 95 units in boiling water at standard pressure. What Celsius temperature corresponds to a reading of 59 units?
questions.explanation: The reading is 54 of the 90 scale units above zero Celsius. Thus the temperature is 100×54/90 = 60°C.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Three vertical rope segments equally support a 210 N load in an ideal pulley system. With ropes and pulleys ideal, how much rope must be pulled to lift the load by 0.8 m?
questions.explanation: All three supporting segments shorten by 0.8 m, so the free end moves through 3×0.8 m.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 25 kg trolley moves at 10 m/s on a horizontal track. A constant 250 N force opposes the motion. How far does the trolley travel before stopping?
questions.explanation: Initial kinetic energy is ½×25×100 = 1,250 J. The braking force uses that energy over 1,250/250 metres.

questions.question: Of the surveyed trips, how many were by bus or bicycle?
questions.explanation: The two sectors span 126° out of 360°. Multiply 480 by 126/360 to obtain 168.

questions.question: Among trips made using train or bus, what percentage were made by train?
questions.explanation: Compare angles within the subset: 162/(162+108) = 60%.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: How many trips were made on foot by passengers who reported a trip of at most 20 minutes?
questions.explanation: Walking represents 480×54/360 = 72 trips. Half of these meet the time condition, giving 36.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: If 24 bus trips switch to train while the total stays fixed, by how many percentage points does the train share increase?
questions.explanation: Moving 24 of 480 trips to train increases its share by 24/480 = 5 percentage points.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: If the original bicycle count doubles and all other counts stay the same, what is the new bicycle-sector angle, rounded to the nearest degree?
questions.explanation: Bicycle trips rise from 24 to 48, and the total becomes 504. The angle is 360×48/504 ≈ 34°.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: How many of the recorded queues had at least 8 passengers?
questions.explanation: Add the frequencies for 8, 12 and 16 passengers: 8+4+2 = 14.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: What was the mean queue size across the 24 observations, to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: The weighted sum is 0×2+4×8+8×8+12×4+16×2 = 176. Divide by 24.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: One queue recorded as having 12 passengers actually had 16. What is the corrected mean queue size to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: The total rises from 176 to 180 with the sample size still 24. The new mean is 180/24 = 7.50.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: What fraction of observations had a queue size strictly below the mean?
questions.explanation: The mean is about 7.33. The values below it are 0 and 4, with frequencies 2 and 8. Thus 10 of 24 observations qualify.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Counters P and Q together sold 280 tickets. How many did P sell? Statement I: P sold 30 more than Q. Statement II: Q sold fewer than 140.
questions.explanation: The sum and difference determine P as 155. An upper bound on Q leaves several possibilities.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three routes handled a total of 420 tickets. What was the count on route A? I: A handled twice as many as B. II: C handled as many as A and B combined.
questions.explanation: II fixes A+B at 210. I then gives B = 70 and A = 140. Neither relation fixes A by itself.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Does counter X sell more tickets per hour than counter Y? I: X sells three times as many tickets as Y. II: X operates twice as many hours as Y. Both counters sell a positive number of tickets.
questions.explanation: Rates require both counts and operating times. The two ratios give X a rate 3/2 times Y’s rate.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Three counters A, B and C sold 70, 90 and 110 tickets in some order. A sold more than B, and C did not sell 70. What is the number sold by B?
questions.explanation: If B sold 90, A would have sold 110 and C would be left with 70. Therefore B sold 70.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: Four services A, B, C and D last 30, 40, 60 and 80 minutes, all different. A takes twice as long as B, C is longer than D, and D is not the shortest. By how many minutes is C longer than D?
questions.explanation: If A and B took 80 and 40, C and D would be 60 and 30, making D the shortest. Thus A and B take 60 and 30, with C at 80 and D at 40. The difference is 40 minutes.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Between 4:00 and the first overlap after it, when is the smaller angle between the clock hands 26.5°?
questions.explanation: On this side of the overlap the separation is 30 × 4 − 5.5m. Set that equal to 26.5 and solve for m = 17.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A register is inspected on a Wednesday. Its next inspection is due 34 days later, but it is carried out two days after the due date. On which weekday is the inspection carried out?
questions.explanation: The actual interval is 36 days. Its remainder on division by seven is 1. Advance that many weekdays from Wednesday.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Kiran and Lata are sisters. The second sister’s husband has a son from an earlier marriage and a daughter with her. What is the first sister’s relationship to that daughter?
questions.explanation: The girl’s mother is the second sister. The mother’s sister is the maternal aunt. The earlier child is unrelated to that identification.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Five containers weigh 6, 8, 11, 15, 21 kg. A loading bay accepts exactly two whose combined weight is exactly 27 kg. The heavier selected container is loaded first. Which weight is loaded second?
questions.explanation: Testing pairs against the capacity leaves 21 + 6 = 27. In descending weight order the second is 6 kg.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A lamp is already on. Each pulse reverses its state. It receives 7 pulses before a pause, then 9 more pulses. During maintenance the technician manually toggles it once and disconnects it before any further pulse. What was its state immediately before the manual toggle and immediately afterwards?
questions.explanation: The total number of automatic toggles is 16. Each pair cancels. The manual toggle then reverses the state once more.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question:
Exactly one of Kiran, Lata, Meena is assigned a report, and exactly 0 of the following claims are true.
1. Kiran is assigned the report.
2. Lata is assigned the report.
3. Meena is not assigned the report.
Who receives the report?
questions.explanation: Test the three possible recipients. Assigning the report to Kiran makes 2 claims true; assigning it to Lata makes 2 claims true; assigning it to Meena makes 0 claims true. Only Meena yields the required count.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An audit reviews 24 requests. A request can pass only if both its date and fare are verified. All requests with verified fares have reference codes. Exactly 6 requests lack a code and 8 requests lack date verification. The two groups overlap in two cases. What is the largest possible number of passes?
questions.explanation: Any request without a code lacks fare verification and therefore fails. The union of the two groups is 6 + 8 − 2 = 12 requests. At most 24 − 12 can pass, and that is possible if all other requests meet both requirements.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Five applicants Vidya, Waseem, Yamini, Zoya and Anil are each on at least one of two lists. List X has three names and List Y has three names. X includes Vidya and Waseem; Y includes Yamini and Zoya. Both lists exclude the two names already given for the other list. Who must appear on both?
questions.explanation: The given members are exclusive. The only remaining applicant, Anil, must fill the third place on both lists.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A surveyor starts facing south, goes 13 m forward, turns left and goes 6 m, then turns left again and goes 10 m. Ignoring obstacles, which displacement from the start is correct?
questions.explanation: The first and third walks are opposite, leaving 13 − 10 = 3 m along the original heading. The middle walk is to the left of the starting direction.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Exactly two of Vidya, Waseem, Yamini and Zoya are on leave. Vidya is on leave if and only if Yamini is on leave. Zoya is working. The two people at work must cover reception and records, one duty each. Zoya covers records. Who covers reception?
questions.explanation: Because Zoya is working and exactly two people are on leave, the paired leave status must put Vidya and Yamini on leave. The working pair is Waseem and Zoya.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Team P inspected 12 boxes and team Q inspected 6 boxes. Exactly 8 of all inspected boxes were rejected. Each team inspected a disjoint set. What is the minimum possible number of rejections from P?
questions.explanation: At most 6 rejections can come from Q because Q inspected only 6. That leaves at least 2 among P. The minimum is attainable if every Q box was rejected.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A committee selects exactly two of reports Vidya, Waseem, Yamini and Zoya. Selecting Vidya forces Yamini. Selecting Zoya rules out Yamini. New rules also forbid choosing Waseem together with Yamini, and forbid choosing Waseem together with Zoya. Which pair can be selected?
questions.explanation: Any pair containing Vidya must also contain Yamini. Without Vidya, all three possible pairs among Waseem, Yamini and Zoya breach a prohibition. The single valid pair is Vidya–Yamini.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: A report uses the example of a queue to explain why a list of waiting tasks can grow even when work speeds up. Which observation best transfers the analogy?
options: The tasks vary in age but not in arrival rate.
Staff change how completed work is labelled.
New tasks arrive faster than the improved processing rate.
The queue is divided into two lines with the same total capacity.
questions.explanation: The waiting stock rises whenever inflow exceeds outflow, even if outflow has increased.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: An app appears to improve completion rates. Users may choose whether to install it, and users with earlier unfinished work are also more likely to install it. What comparison best examines the app’s effect?
options: Offer access randomly among users with comparable unfinished work and compare their later results.
Compare users on the app by the time of day they install it.
Compare current app users with a different group from an earlier year.
Count how many downloads occur after a publicity campaign.
questions.explanation: Randomising access within a comparable group addresses the imbalance in users’ prior unfinished work.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which order satisfies every clue, from position 1 to position 5?
questions.explanation: Checking the stated restrictions leaves only Charu → Esha → Bina → Deepa → Asha. Asha → Charu → Bina → Deepa → Esha violates clue 2. Asha → Charu → Bina → Esha → Deepa violates clue 2. Bina → Charu → Asha → Deepa → Esha violates clue 1.
questions.passage:
Five colleagues are assigned one each to desks numbered 1–5 from left to right.
1. Bina works at desk 3.
2. Asha works two desks to the right of Bina.
3. Charu has a lower desk number than Esha.
4. Esha is not immediately to the left of Asha.
5. Deepa sits to the right of Charu.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: If clue 1 is dropped and all other clues still apply, how many orders are possible?
questions.explanation: Retain all clues except 1. The remaining constraints admit 18 distinct permutations, including the original order. Count arrangements with position 1 fixed before moving to the next permitted first item.
questions.passage:
Five candidates are ranked 1 through 5 by score. All scores differ.
1. Jaya ranks above Indu and exactly one position separates them.
2. Hema is lower than Indu but is more than one position below Indu.
3. Gita ranks higher than Farah.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: How does the historian distinguish the claims she can make?
options: She treats the household accounts as unreliable wherever port records are silent.
She uses the range of canvas prices to estimate differences in repair labour.
She separates evidence that the work occurred from evidence of individual earnings.
She gives descendant accounts decisive weight in calculating port-wide incomes.
questions.explanation: The evidence recovers an activity without consistently identifying the worker or payment per worker.
questions.passage: A historian studying a former port found that its official ledgers recorded almost nothing about the women who repaired sailcloth. After interviewing descendants and examining household accounts, she found scattered entries for thread, damaged canvas, and payments made on delivery. These entries illuminated work the ledgers had ignored, though they rarely showed how labour was divided within a household. She therefore refused to estimate individual wages. The evidence, she argued, was strong enough to change an account of who sustained the port, but too uneven to support a precise estimate of what each worker earned.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which discovery would most directly address the historian’s stated limit?
options: A larger ledger listing the quantities of sailcloth entering the port.
A map giving the locations of households that traded with the port.
An interview describing how many repairs a typical sail required in winter.
A series of receipts listing named workers, repair jobs and their individual payments.
questions.explanation: Linked names, tasks and amounts would support estimates of individual pay. The other discoveries add context without supplying that link.
questions.passage: A historian studying a former port found that its official ledgers recorded almost nothing about the women who repaired sailcloth. After interviewing descendants and examining household accounts, she found scattered entries for thread, damaged canvas, and payments made on delivery. These entries illuminated work the ledgers had ignored, though they rarely showed how labour was divided within a household. She therefore refused to estimate individual wages. The evidence, she argued, was strong enough to change an account of who sustained the port, but too uneven to support a precise estimate of what each worker earned.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: What role do the entries for thread and damaged canvas play?
options: They establish the earliest year in which repair work was undertaken.
They indicate that families held contracts to manufacture new sails.
They show that households recorded payment consistently for each worker.
They provide indirect traces of the repair work absent from official accounts.
questions.explanation: The entries reveal inputs and transactions associated with repairs, but give limited detail about the people doing them.
questions.passage: A historian studying a former port found that its official ledgers recorded almost nothing about the women who repaired sailcloth. After interviewing descendants and examining household accounts, she found scattered entries for thread, damaged canvas, and payments made on delivery. The evidence, she argued, was strong enough to change an account of who sustained the port, but too uneven to support a precise estimate of what each worker earned.

questions.subject: Logical Capability
questions.question: Which heading would fit the passage most closely?
options: Recovering missing labour from incomplete records
Why household accounts displaced port ledgers
Measuring changes in the price of sailcloth
Reconstructing a complete wage series from oral history
questions.explanation: The passage is about recovering overlooked labour and respecting the limits of uneven records.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A code transforms STONE into HKLQV. First it shifts the two end letters forward by 3 and the three inside letters back by 3. What does the same code produce for CROWN, if it then reverses the shifted letters?
questions.explanation: The shifted intermediate word is FOLTQ. Its reversal is QTLOF.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a cipher STONE becomes UVNPD and GUIDE becomes ITHFD. The rule depends on whether the original letter is a vowel. How is CROWN encoded?
questions.explanation: From the examples, a vowel goes back one letter, and a consonant goes forward two letters. Classify each original letter separately.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: To encode a word, write its last, first and middle letters in that order as alphabet positions (A = 1). Replace each successive number after the first with its sum with the preceding original number. If the result is 14 / 17 / 18, what are the original first, middle and last letters in that order?
questions.explanation: The first displayed number gives the last letter. Subtract it from the second number to recover the first letter. Subtract the recovered first-letter value from the third to recover the middle letter.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A five-letter code sends STONE to TVRRJ and PLANT to QNDRY. What code does it give CROWN?
questions.explanation: Reading two examples reveals successive shifts +1, +2, +3, +4 and +5. Apply those position shifts to CROWN and wrap after Z.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: On odd positions a code advances the letter by 3. On even positions it uses A↔Z, B↔Y, and so on. Which plain word produces FIRDQ?
questions.explanation: Move odd-position letters backward by the stated shift. Mirroring is its own inverse at even positions.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In each pair (p,q) value one place apart gives (4,5) → 9 and (7,8) → 15. Check also (5,8) → 39. Under the same relation, what is (9,12)?
questions.explanation: The relation is q² − p² = (q − p)(q + p). The three-unit gap multiplies the sum of the two entries.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: The rule sends 4 to 17, 7 to 47, and 9 to 77. It multiplies each input by one less than itself and adds a fixed constant. Which input gives 25?
questions.explanation: The examples establish the constant as 5. Subtract it from the target, then identify the adjacent factors. The larger factor is the input.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A machine transforms 18 to 6 and 50 to 10 by replacing an integer with the product of its distinct prime factors. If 108 is passed through the machine, and its output is passed through again, what is the final result?
questions.explanation: The first pass multiplies one copy of each distinct prime to give 6. The second pass sees exactly those same primes, each already present once.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Pairs 5 → 16 and 6 → 21 use the same rule. The rule uses the sum of the first n positive numbers, adjusted only when n is odd. Which output is paired with 13?
questions.explanation: An even input gives n(n+1)/2. The odd example is one larger than its triangular number, so add one only when the new input is odd.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: For a two-digit number with unequal digits, 27 corresponds to 45 and 41 corresponds to 27. The output is the positive difference between the number and its reversal. Which input has the same output as 47?
questions.explanation: The difference is nine times the absolute digit gap. 4 and 7 differ by 3; both digits can increase by one without changing that gap.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: H ranks 18th in a preliminary list. The final list removes two people originally above H and adds 6 new entries. The number of new entries above H is half the new entries, rounded down. What is H’s final rank?
questions.explanation: Remove two higher ranks and add the stated number of newly higher ranks. Removed or added entries below H do not change H’s position.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Six runners have distinct times. S is faster than W but slower than T and P. U is faster than T and P is slower than T. W is faster than V. If the times of P and W are swapped, who is at rank 3, where rank 1 is fastest?
questions.explanation: The original order is U, T, P, S, W, V. The swap gives U, T, W, S, P, V. Read rank 3 from the new order.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a list of 44, K ranks 11th from the front and L ranks 15th from the rear. M ranks midway between them, counting positions. If their two positions have different parity, use the central position closer to K. What is M’s rank from the rear?
questions.explanation: L is at position 30 from the front. The lower of the central positions is 20. Convert it to the reverse rank by subtracting from 44 and adding 1.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A list ranks higher score first. For tied scores, earlier submission wins. K scores 18 at 09:21, L scores 30 at 09:24, M scores 30 at 09:18, and N scores 18 at 09:14. Two entries from each score band are initially listed. If M’s time is corrected to 09:29, which consecutive pair occupies places 2 and 3, in order?
questions.explanation: L now leads M in the higher-score band. N leads K in the lower-score band. The order is L, M, N, K.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a queue of 44, H is 11th from the front and J is 15th from the back. They swap places and everyone faces the other way, reversing which end is the front. How many people are ahead of J in the new direction?
questions.explanation: J moves to H’s old position. Under reversal the 33 people formerly behind that slot are now ahead.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: In a row of 44, H is 11th from the left and J is 15th from the right, with J right of H. Three people between them leave. Two new people join left of H. How many now stand between H and J?
questions.explanation: J began at position 30 from the left, so the gap contained 18 people. Only the three removals affect that gap.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Each value from the third onward is the sum of the previous two. In the display 6, ?, 13, 20, 33, 53, what value must replace the question mark?
questions.explanation: Subtract the first term 6 from the third term 13. The answer 7 also gives the correct fourth term when added to the third.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: A register displays 6, 13, 38, 77, 230, 461 using the same two affine operations in alternation. Which value is first to exceed 1381 if the pattern continues?
questions.explanation: Apply ×2 + 1, then ×3 − 1, alternately. The sixth term uses the ×2 rule, so the seventh is 3 × 461 − 1 = 1382.

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Complete both blanks in this sequence: 6, 30, 8, 29, 12, 26, __, __.
questions.explanation: Odd positions increase by consecutive even numbers (+2, +4, +6). Even positions decrease by consecutive odd numbers (−1, −3, −5).

questions.subject: Mental Reasoning
questions.question: Find the missing interior term in 6, 8, ?, 20, 36, 68, 132.
questions.explanation: The gaps double: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64. Add 4 to the second term to get 12.

title: RRB Station Master CBT · Practice model 3
note: Full-length CBT practice with multi-step maths and science, shared data sets, English comprehension and reasoning. Uses the indicative 30/30/20/20 breakdown of CEN 08/2026.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 40 L tank contains a well-mixed 30% solution. Ten litres are removed and replaced by 10 L of a 50% solution. What is the final concentration?
questions.explanation: The remaining 30 L contains 9 L of solute. The replacement adds 5 L, giving 14 L in 40 L.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A town’s annual ridership increases by 25% one year and falls by 16% the next year. What is the net change over the two years?
questions.explanation: The factors multiply: 1.25×0.84 = 1.05.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A small depot handles 60 consignments with mean processing time 12 minutes and a larger depot handles 90 with mean time 20 minutes. Nine consignments at the larger depot took 10 minutes each and are excluded. What is the mean processing time of the remaining 141 consignments to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: The adjusted total is 60×12+90×20−9×10 = 2,430 minutes, and 2,430/141 ≈ 17.23.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 12 hours. A leak can empty the full tank in 18 hours. At constant rates, how long will the pipe take to fill the remaining two-thirds of the tank with the leak open?
questions.explanation: The net rate is 1/12−1/18 = 1/36 tank per hour. Filling two-thirds takes (2/3)×36 hours.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two runners start together on a 360 m circular track and run in opposite directions at constant speeds of 5 m/s and 7 m/s. How long after starting do they first meet again?
questions.explanation: The two runners together cover one lap at a combined speed of 12 m/s. Divide 360 by 12.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two trains 180 m and 220 m long move towards each other at 54 and 90 km/h. How long do they take to pass each other completely, starting when the fronts meet?
questions.explanation: The closing speed is 144 km/h = 40 m/s. Both lengths, totalling 400 m, must pass.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A supplier sells two items for ₹960 each. On one it gains 20% and on the other it loses 20%. What is its overall result?
questions.explanation: The cost prices are ₹800 and ₹1,200, totalling ₹2,000. The ₹1,920 received is 4% lower.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: An older sibling is 6 years older than a younger sibling. Four years ago the older sibling was twice the age of the younger one. What is the sum of their current ages?
questions.explanation: If the younger sibling is x, then x+2 = 2(x−4), so x = 10. Their current ages sum to 26.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A hall has 16 rows. The first has 12 seats, and each successive row has 7 more seats than the previous one. How many seats are in the hall?
questions.explanation: The last row has 12+15×7 = 117 seats. Multiply the average of the first and last rows by 16.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: What is the remainder when 2 to the ninth power multiplied by 3 to the fifth power is divided by 7?
questions.explanation: Since 2³ leaves remainder 1, so does 2⁹. The remainder of 3⁵ is 5 because 3²≡2 and 3⁴≡4 modulo 7.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that their sum is 9 or that both dice show the same number?
questions.explanation: Four ordered outcomes sum to 9 and six are doubles. The two events are disjoint, giving 10/36.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A bag holds 3 white and 5 black counters. Two counters are drawn independently with replacement. What is the probability of drawing at least one white counter?
questions.explanation: The probability of two black draws is (5/8)² = 25/64. Subtract it from one.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: At the same moment on level ground, a vertical 1.6 m post casts a 2.4 m shadow and a tower casts an 18 m shadow. What is the tower’s height?
questions.explanation: The height-to-shadow ratio is shared because the sun’s elevation is the same. Multiply 18 by 1.6/2.4.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: In an 8 m square, a quarter circle of radius 4 m is drawn inside each corner. The quarter circles touch without overlapping. What area lies outside all four sectors?
questions.explanation: Four quarter circles make one complete radius-4 circle, of area 16π m². Subtract it from 64 m².

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Water fills a pipe of radius 2 cm and moves at 25 m/min. At what rate is water delivered in litres per minute?
questions.explanation: The cross-section is 4π cm² and the speed is 2,500 cm/min. The resulting 10,000π cm³/min is 10π L/min.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A dataset is 4, 7, 9, 12, 13 and 15. If the largest value is changed to 45, by how much do the mean and median increase respectively?
questions.explanation: The total increases by 30 across six values. The middle two observations remain 9 and 12.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Which expression gives the SI unit of pressure in terms of kilograms, metres and seconds?
questions.explanation: Pressure is force divided by area. Dividing kg·m/s² by m² gives kg/(m·s²).

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: In an insulated vessel, 200 g of water at 70°C is mixed with 300 g of water at 20°C. Neglect the heat capacity of the vessel. What is the equilibrium temperature?
questions.explanation: Equal specific heats make the final temperature the mass-weighted average: (200×70+300×20)/500.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two blocks of equal mass receive the same amount of heat. Block X warms up by 18°C and block Y by 12°C, with no heat losses. What is the ratio of X’s specific heat capacity to Y’s?
questions.explanation: Specific heat capacity is inversely proportional to the rise when added heat and mass are the same.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 4 Ω resistor and an 8 Ω resistor are in series across an ideal 24 V source. What power is dissipated in the 8 Ω resistor?
questions.explanation: The circuit current is 24/(4+8) = 2 A. The 8 Ω resistor dissipates I²R = 32 W.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 1.2 kW appliance operates for 45 minutes each day for 20 days. At ₹7.50 per kWh, what is its energy cost?
questions.explanation: The energy used is 1.2×0.75×20 = 18 kWh, costing 18×7.50.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 20 kg box slides along a level floor with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.25. With g = 10 m/s², how much work does friction do while the box moves 6 m?
questions.explanation: The friction force is 0.25×200 = 50 N. Its work is negative because it opposes the 6 m displacement.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 2 kg cart moves at 4 m/s. A net force transfers another 20 J of energy into its kinetic energy. What is the new speed?
questions.explanation: Initial kinetic energy is 16 J. The new kinetic energy is 36 J and equals v² for a 2 kg cart.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two identical loads are lifted the same vertical distance at constant speed. Motor A takes 24 s and motor B takes 18 s. What is the ratio of B’s useful power to A’s useful power?
questions.explanation: The work is the same, so the power ratio is the inverse time ratio 24:18.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A real machine lifts a 360 N load by 0.8 m while its input point moves 3 m. If its efficiency is 80%, what input force is needed along the motion?
questions.explanation: The useful work is 288 J. Input work is 288/0.8 = 360 J, requiring 120 N over 3 m.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A rectangular metal block measures 10 cm by 5 cm by 4 cm. A 2 cm by 5 cm by 4 cm piece is cut out. The density is 7.5 g/cm³. What is the remaining mass?
questions.explanation: Volume falls from 200 to 160 cm³. Multiply by 7.5 g/cm³ to get 1,200 g.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A trolley covers 30 m in the first 5 s and 24 m in the next 3 s. What is its average speed over the full motion?
questions.explanation: The total distance is 54 m in 8 s, giving 54/8 = 6.75 m/s.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: Two resistors of 6 Ω and 12 Ω are connected in parallel to an ideal source. What is the ratio of their dissipated powers, 6 Ω to 12 Ω?
questions.explanation: Their voltages are equal. Power is V²/R, so the 6 Ω resistor dissipates twice the power.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 2.0 m rail expands by 0.024 mm per degree Celsius over the temperature range considered. How long is it after a 50°C rise?
questions.explanation: The increase is 0.024×50 = 1.2 mm or 0.0012 m.

questions.subject: Basic Science and Mathematics
questions.question: A 120 N load is 0.30 m to the left of a frictionless pivot. A second 60 N load is 0.20 m to the right. How far to the right must an additional 80 N load be placed to balance the lever?
questions.explanation: The left moment is 36 N·m and the existing right moment is 12 N·m. The remaining 24 N·m requires a 0.30 m arm for 80 N.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: How many surveyed workers attended none of the courses?
questions.explanation: The union is 78+70+65−35−28−25+12 = 137. Subtract from 160.
questions.table:

Pairs including anyone who attended all three: A and B = 35, B and C = 28, A and C = 25.

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: How many workers attended exactly two of the courses?
questions.explanation: The sum of pair counts is 88 and counts the triple intersection three times. Subtract 36 to get 52.
questions.table:

questions.subject: Data Analysis
questions.question: How many workers attended exactly one course?
questions.explanation: The union of 137 consists of exactly one, exactly two and exactly three. Subtract 52 and 12.

questions.question: Among workers who attended course A, what fraction also attended course B?
questions.explanation: The inclusive A-and-B count is 35 out of the 78 A attendees.
